definition: Naturalization power is the authority of Congress under Article I, Section 8, Clause 4 of the Constitution "[t]o establish a uniform rule of naturalization." Congress has the sole power to create laws over naturalization; meaning Congress passes laws deciding who may become a citizen and the process of obtaining citizenship. Exercising its naturalization power, Congress passed the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Naturalization law and procedure must follow the INA. As immigration is a federal legislative issue, courts and state legislatures cannot change the INA. See naturalization and congressional power.
